registry.description: Obedience is the act of doing what one has been told by someone with authority over one — the concrete expression of submission and trust in the one who commands. The Greek vocabulary here is precise: the word means to listen under, suggesting that obedience begins with hearing. Obedience in Scripture is not blind compliance but the response of trust: because God's commands are good and his character is trustworthy, doing what he says is the appropriate response. Christ's own obedience to the Father is the supreme model.
